back: Point: one odd value. Contextual: odd given its context (season, location). Collective: a group is odd although each element is not.
Anomalies are rare and ever-changing, so labelled examples are scarce; anything unlike normal is suspicious, including unseen types.
$z=(x-\mu)/\sigma$; flag $|z|>3$. Assumes roughly Gaussian data and suffers masking.
Outliers inflate the mean and standard deviation, which hides them from the test. Fix: median and MAD.
$D(x)=\sqrt{(x-\mu)^\top\Sigma^{-1}(x-\mu)}$: Euclidean distance after whitening; mean of $D^2$ is about $d$ for Gaussian data.
Mean and covariance are contaminated by outliers, $\Sigma$ may be singular ($d>N$ or collinear features), and it assumes one elliptical blob.
Random cuts isolate anomalies in few splits; score by the average path length over many trees.
Random feature, uniform threshold between node min and max, depth limit $\lceil\log_2\psi\rceil$, subsample $\psi$ (often 256).
$c(n)=2(\ln(n-1)+0.5772)-2(n-1)/n$, the average unsuccessful-search path in a binary search tree; $c(2)=1$.
$s(x)=2^{-E[h(x)]/c(\psi)}$: near 1 anomalous, about 0.5 average, well below 0.5 very normal.
Ratio of neighbours' local density to the point's own density; about 1 normal, much above 1 an outlier in a locally dense region.
It only sets the threshold (flag the top fraction); it does not change the scores.
Precision@k, PR-AUC, synthetic injections, stability across seeds, rank agreement and human feedback; evaluate on later data.
